newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations steady, but Italy down - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations steady, but Italy down - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of European monetary union starting on time were little changed over the past week, with the only significant decline being in Italy, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
Market prices indicate that the perceived probabilities of countries like Spain, Sweden, Finland and Ireland joining Germany in EMU in 1999 remained close last week's levels, the calculator showed.
The probability of Italy taking part, however, dropped five percentage points to 50 percent and is now down 11 points over the past month.
Over the past month, prices show EMU expectations have been scaled back about six points in Spain. Finland, Denmark and the UK are the only countries to register significant advances over four weeks.
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week and last month, the calculator showed.
JP Morgan said it added Finland, Portugal and Ireland to its calculations for the first time this week.

The U.S. investment house also pointed out that it is reasonable to estimate a margin of error in probability levels of three-to-five points, due to reliability of historical data or faults in the model.
In the case of Ireland, however, a shortage of historical 10-year swap data may mean a margin of error of about 10 points.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
